overall: Violation found for failing to timely approve the October 4 minutes (approved only in March 2022; staffing shortages not good cause). No violation for cancelled meetings or post-meeting notice revisions; untimely notice claim declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to approve minutes of its October 4, November 1, and December 6 meetings in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Board concedes, and we find, that the Board failed to approve its October 4 meeting minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Minutes for the cancelled November 1 and December 6 meetings were not approved on time, as alleged in the same complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, because the Board did not meet on November 1 and December 6, we find no violation for failing to approve minutes for the meetings which were cancelled.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board improperly amended six meeting notices months after the meetings took place.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not regulate what public bodies may do with meeting notices after the meeting has passed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that during a November 22 open session the Board admitted it met without posting prior notice.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation because it is untimely as the complaint was filed on February 22, 2022, more than 30 days after the alleged violation could reasonably be discovered.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
